text: What is the bright star in the eastern sky this morning? It's Venus. The very bright "star" low in the east before sunrise in November 2026 is the planet Venus. It is the brightest object in the predawn sky after the Moon, at about magnitude -4.5 to -4.7. Higher up, in the south-southeast, the bright point is Jupiter, with fainter, reddish Mars close beside it.. Venus became a brilliant morning star in early November 2026, while Mars and Jupiter meet in a close conjunction before dawn on Nov. 16.. Venus has returned to the morning sky as the "morning star." Astronomy magazine lists it at about magnitude -4.5 on Nov. 7 and -4.7 on Nov. 11, 2026, and says its backward (retrograde) motion against the stars ends on Nov. 11 at 10 a.m. EST. Through a telescope it currently shows a thin crescent, about 14% lit. In mid-November it sits roughly 15 degrees above the east-southeast horizon an hour before sunrise, close to Spica, the brightest star in Virgo. Mercury is also low in the east-southeast, to Venus's lower left. Jupiter is the second-brightest point in the morning sky. It is high in the south-southeast before dawn in the constellation Leo, a few degrees from Regulus, Leo's brightest star. Mars has been closing in on Jupiter all autumn; the two pass about a degree apart, with the closest approach around Nov. 14 to 17 and the conjunction on Nov. 16, 2026. Mars looks much fainter and slightly orange. The best time to look is about an hour before sunrise. Planets usually shine with a steadier light than stars, which tend to twinkle.

How are the CMA Awards voted on? Who picks the 2026 winners. CMA Awards nominees and winners are chosen by the Country Music Association's more than 7,000 professional members, including artists, songwriters, musicians, executives, publicists and touring staff. They vote in three rounds by emailed ballot. For 2026, the final ballot closed Oct. 27, and winners are revealed live on ABC on Nov. 18.. The 60th CMA Awards air on ABC on Nov. 18, 2026, three weeks after CMA members cast their final ballots.. According to the CMA, only its Professional voting members can vote. The 2026 nomination ballot ran July 6-16, the second ballot Aug. 4-17 and the final ballot Oct. 1-27, with each round closing at 6 p.m. Central on its last day. Music released between July 1, 2025, and June 30, 2026, was eligible, and the CMA Board of Directors sets the rules. Fans do not vote in the CMA Awards. The 60th annual CMA Awards air live from Nashville on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, at 8 p.m. ET (7 p.m. Central) on ABC, the show's home since 2006. Lainey Wilson returns as host. Ella Langley leads the nominations with nine. The Entertainer of the Year nominees are Luke Combs, Cody Johnson, Ella Langley, Chris Stapleton and Lainey Wilson. The New Artist of the Year nominees are Avery Anna, Carter Faith, Emily Ann Roberts, Tucker Wetmore and Stephen Wilson Jr.

How are The Game Awards nominees chosen? The 2026 jury rules. Nominees for The Game Awards are picked by a jury of more than 100 media and influencer outlets worldwide. Each outlet submits one confidential, unranked ballot with five picks per category, and the five games named on the most ballots become the nominees. Fans do not vote on nominations; they only help decide winners.. The Game Awards will announce its 2026 nominees in mid-November, a few days before the Nov. 20 eligibility cutoff, which falls one day after Grand Theft Auto VI's scheduled Nov. 19 release.. According to the show's official FAQ, each jury ballot is meant to reflect the outlet's whole editorial staff. If two games tie for the last spot, the category gets six or more nominees. A few categories, including esports, accessibility and best adaptation, are chosen by separate specialist juries instead of the main panel. Winners are decided by a blend of the same jury (90%) and public fan voting on TheGameAwards.com (10%). For 2026, a game must be commercially available by 9 p.m. PT on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026, to be eligible; for the fan-voted Players' Voice award, it must ship by Nov. 30. Fan voting closes at 6 p.m. PT on Wednesday, Dec. 9. The 2026 show streams live on Thursday, Dec. 10, 2026, from the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, starting at 7:30 p.m. ET (4:30 p.m. PT). The official site says only that 2026 nominees are "coming mid-November"; from 2022 through 2025, nominees were revealed on a Monday in mid-November. Show creator Geoff Keighley does not vote on nominees or winners.

Is Philomena Cunk a real person? Who plays her in Cunk on Cinema. No. Philomena Cunk is a fictional character played by English comedian Diane Morgan. She is a deadpan, cheerfully clueless presenter in mockumentaries written by Charlie Brooker. The experts she interviews, however, are real people. Her new series, Cunk on Cinema, streams on Netflix starting Nov. 15, 2026.. Netflix releases "Cunk on Cinema," the latest Philomena Cunk mockumentary, on Nov. 15, 2026.. Cunk first appeared in 2013 on the BBC's "Charlie Brooker's Weekly Wipe." She went on to front "Cunk on Britain" (2018), "Cunk on Earth" (2022) and the special "Cunk on Life" (December 2024). Diane Morgan, born Oct. 5, 1975, in Farnworth, Greater Manchester, England, is also known for playing Liz in "Motherland," Kath in Netflix's "After Life" and for writing and starring in "Mandy." In "Cunk on Cinema," Cunk tackles film history from the invention of the camera to AI. Charlie Brooker created the series with Morgan and leads the writing team. What's on Netflix lists 23 real interviewees, among them director Michael Bay, actor Benedict Cumberbatch, composer Daniel Pemberton, "Die Hard" screenwriter Steven E. De Souza, cinematographer Seamus McGarvey, critic Mark Kermode and physicist Jim Al-Khalili. The joke of the format is that the experts answer her odd questions straight. The name is sometimes misspelled "Philomena Kunk" or "Cunk on Cinemas."

What is a lame duck president? The term, explained. A lame duck president is one whose time in office has a known end date, so his influence is expected to fade. The term is used for a president who lost re-election or did not run, in the weeks before a successor takes over, and more broadly for a president in a second term, who cannot run again under the 22nd Amendment.. "Lame duck" is in the news as Congress returns for its post-election lame duck session on Nov. 9, 2026, after midterms in which Democrats won both chambers.. The 22nd Amendment says "no person shall be elected to the office of the President more than twice," and someone who served more than two years of another president's term can be elected only once. Congress proposed it on March 24, 1947, and it was ratified on Feb. 27, 1951, after Franklin D. Roosevelt won four presidential elections. Britannica notes that presidents who win a second term are often called lame ducks and that the race to succeed them often starts even before their second inauguration. The phrase "lame duck" was first used in 18th-century Britain for bankrupt businessmen, and by the 1830s it was applied to officeholders whose time in office had a known end. The same idea gives the "lame duck session" of Congress, which meets after a November election but before the new Congress is sworn in on Jan. 3. Donald Trump began his second, nonconsecutive term on Jan. 20, 2025, so under the 22nd Amendment he cannot be elected president again; his term ends at noon on Jan. 20, 2029. Separately, the outgoing Congress began its lame duck session on Nov. 9, 2026, after midterms in which, Democrats won control of both chambers.

Are national parks free on Veterans Day 2026? Yes, with a new limit. Yes. On Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026, Veterans Day, the National Park Service waives entrance fees at parks that normally charge them. Starting in 2026, though, fee-free days apply only to U.S. Citizens and residents. International visitors still pay, including a new $100 nonresident fee at 11 popular parks.. Nov. 11, 2026, is the final national park fee-free day of the year and the first Veterans Day under the 2026 rule limiting free entry to U.S. Citizens and residents.. Nov. 11 is the last of the National Park Service's 2026 free entrance days. The others were Feb. 16 (Presidents Day), May 25 (Memorial Day), June 14 (Flag Day), July 3-5 (Independence Day weekend), Aug. 25 (the Park Service's birthday), Sept. 17 (Constitution Day) and Oct. 27 (Theodore Roosevelt's birthday). The NPS passes page says: "Beginning in 2026, free entrance on these days will be for US citizens and residents only." The waiver covers entrance fees only; Yosemite notes that timed-entry or reservation fees may still apply. Nonresidents age 16 and older now pay $100 on top of the regular entrance fee at Acadia, Bryce Canyon, Everglades, Glacier, Grand Canyon, Grand Teton, Rocky Mountain, Sequoia & Kings Canyon, Yellowstone, Yosemite and Zion. That fee is waived for holders of an America the Beautiful pass. The annual pass costs $80 for U.S. Residents and $250 for nonresidents. Veterans and Gold Star Family members can get a free Military Lifetime Pass, and current U.S. Military members and their dependents get a free Military Annual Pass, so they can enter free all year.

What are the new SNAP rules for stores? The 2026 stocking standards. Stores that accept SNAP food stamps must now stock at least seven varieties of staple food in each of four categories: protein, grains, vegetables or fruits, and dairy. That is up from three. The USDA rule took effect July 7, 2026, and stores had to comply by Nov. 4, 2026.. The Nov. 4, 2026, compliance deadline for the USDA's tougher SNAP retailer stocking standards has just passed.. The USDA's Food and Nutrition Service published the final rule, "Updated Staple Food Stocking Standards for Retailers in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program," in the Federal Register on May 8, 2026. Stores must carry 28 staple varieties in total, with at least three stocking units of each variety (84 items). At least one variety in three of the four categories must be perishable, up from two categories before. Plant-based proteins count as protein, and plant-based dairy alternatives can count for up to three dairy varieties. Snacks and desserts such as chips, candy and baked goods do not count as staple foods, and neither do most drinks (milk, certain milk alternatives and 100% juice are exceptions), condiments, sweeteners, spices, cooking oils or butter. Hot or cold prepared foods made in the store do not count either; pre-cut produce does. The rule applies to stores that qualify under the USDA's "Criterion A." New stores are checked when they apply, and existing stores are checked at reauthorization, which generally happens every five years, though the agency can review a store at any time. A store that fails the standards can be denied or lose its authorization and must wait six months to reapply. The rule sets what authorized stores must carry; it is not a rule about which items recipients may buy or how much they receive.

What is a Quarter Quell? The Hunger Games twist, explained. In Suzanne Collins' Hunger Games books, a Quarter Quell is a special edition of the Hunger Games held every 25 years, with an extra twist meant to remind the districts of the Capitol's power. Sunrise on the Reaping, which opens in theaters Nov. 20, 2026, is set during the Second Quarter Quell, the 50th Games.. "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping," the film about Haymitch's Second Quarter Quell, opens in theaters on Nov. 20, 2026.. There are three Quarter Quells in the series. For the first, the 25th Games, the districts had to choose their own tributes instead of holding the random reaping. For the second, the 50th Games, each district sent double the usual number of tributes, 48 in all, with only one victor. For the third, the 75th Games in "Catching Fire," President Snow ordered that tributes be reaped from past victors, sending Katniss and Peeta back into the arena. Haymitch Abernathy, Katniss' mentor in the original trilogy, won the 50th Games, the Second Quarter Quell. In "Sunrise on the Reaping," his reaping takes place on his 16th birthday. Scholastic published the novel on March 18, 2025. Lionsgate's film adaptation, "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping," is directed by Francis Lawrence and stars Joseph Zada as young Haymitch. It opens in U.S. Theaters on Nov. 20, 2026. The term is sometimes misspelled "quarter quel" or "quarter quill."

What is Apple HomeView? Apple's $299 smart display, explained. Apple HomeView is Apple's first smart home display: a $299 device with a 7-inch square screen and speaker that controls smart home gadgets, plays music, makes FaceTime calls and runs Apple's new Siri AI. Apple announced it on Oct. 13, 2026, and it goes on sale in the U.S. On Friday, Nov. 13, 2026.. Apple's HomeView smart display, announced Oct. 13, 2026, goes on sale in the U.S. On Nov. 13.. HomeView comes in two versions at the same $299 price: a tabletop model on a domed speaker base with a tilting stainless steel hinge, and a wall-mounted model. According to 9to5Mac, the tabletop version comes in silver, starlight, rose pink and space gray, and the wall version in space gray and silver. Wall mounts made with Schneider Home start at $59.95 for a USB-C connector and $79.95 for an AC wired mount; a $129.95 Power over Ethernet mount is due in early 2027. The 7-inch Liquid Retina display reaches 500 nits and can dim to 0.3 nits for a nightstand. A Center Stage front camera handles FaceTime calls. The device recognizes up to six people and shows each one a personal Home Screen with their messages, calendar and contacts. Preloaded apps include Calendar, Messages, Photos, FaceTime, Notes, Reminders, Music and Podcasts. It works by touch or voice, has an intercom feature and can show up to nine home camera feeds at once. Siri on HomeView can view camera feeds, adjust a thermostat, turn on lights and lock doors. People with an Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone or iPad get Siri answers that use their personal context. 9to5Mac reports HomeView will not be sold in the European Union, where Apple's Siri AI is not available.

What is Pico Park? The co-op game behind Sonic Pico Park. Pico Park is a cooperative puzzle-platformer from the Japanese indie studio TECOPARK in which every player must work together to reach the goal. It first came out on Steam on April 26, 2016. A Sonic the Hedgehog version, Sonic Pico Park, launches Nov. 12, 2026, for 2 to 8 players.. Sonic Pico Park, a Sonic the Hedgehog take on the Pico Park co-op series, releases on Nov. 12, 2026.. In Pico Park, players control small, identical characters, and no one can finish a stage alone: the group has to cooperate to solve each puzzle and reach the goal. The game later came to Nintendo Switch. The current version supports 2 to 8 players, and the free Classic Edition supported up to 10. Wikipedia credits a developer known as Teco as its designer, programmer and artist, and estimates the game has sold more than 230,000 copies. A sequel, Pico Park 2, came out on Switch on Aug. 27, 2024, and on PC and Xbox on Sept. 12, 2024. The free Pico Park: Classic Edition was pulled from the Steam store on June 14, 2026, after TECOPARK announced its removal on June 1. Sonic Pico Park, also written "SONIC PICO PARK," blends the series with Sega's Sonic games: every character can use Sonic's Spin Dash, and stages add rings, loops and springs. Players reach the goal plate at the right side of each stage. It releases Nov. 12, 2026, on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch 2, Nintendo Switch and PC (Steam), with local and online play and online cross-play.
